clue.text: Company returning to occupy former site

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: late as in 'the late chairman', meaning former

indicators.note: something returning heads back the way it came, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: standard abbreviation for company, reversed here

explanation.surface: A business moving back into premises it used to own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Site' is a verb here, as in to site a factory; 'former site' reads as a noun phrase but splits after 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something and to locate it both mean to place it in a particular position.

clue.text: Past French leader in America touring a state there

parts.note: Louis was the name of many former kings of France

indicators.note: touring a place means travelling around it, so these letters surround another

parts.note: 'in' as written, plus A for America
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former French ruler travelling round an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'state there' leans on 'America' earlier in the clue to fix which country's state is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the United States, named after the French king Louis XIV.

clue.text: Rust in part of reactor containing fuel cylinder?

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside

parts.note: the core is the central part of a nuclear reactor
a fuel rod is the cylinder holding nuclear fuel

explanation.surface: Rust forming inside the part of a reactor that holds a fuel cylinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to wear away by chemical action, and to rust is the same process in iron.

clue.text: Confidential place for prayer session set up?

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means lifted upward, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: terce is the church service said at the third hour of the day
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: A query about a private spot arranged for a prayer meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Terce is one of the canonical hours, the fixed daily offices of monastic prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Top secret is the highest classification for confidential information.

clue.text: Jane is disheartened by a rotten feeling of resentment

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle of the name drops out, leaving only its ends

parts.note: the name with its middle letters removed
'by' places the next piece alongside; 'a' is taken as written
lousy means very bad or rotten

explanation.surface: Jane is downcast because of a nasty sense of grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is resentment towards a rival or someone who has what you want; the clue's phrase is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Being evasive, erroneously give caution about question

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters surround another
something done erroneously is done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
Q is the standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly issues a warning over a query, dodging the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivocating means using vague language to avoid committing oneself, which is being evasive.

clue.text: Pin supported by old bricks?

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A pin held up by aged brickwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supported by' puts the second piece underneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the toy construction system made of small plastic bricks; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: City's culture only periodically considered authentic

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
echt, borrowed from German, means genuine or authentic

explanation.surface: A city's culture is only now and then thought genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a city in the central Netherlands, capital of the province of the same name.

clue.text: How you may get a rise out of people voting for Trump at first

definitions.text: How you may get a rise

parts.note: the yeas are those voting in favour

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A way of provoking Trump's supporters into anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a rise out of' is an idiom for provoking someone, but here the rise is dough swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the leavening agent that makes bread dough rise.

clue.text: Tear into quinces (occasionally still green, perhaps)

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means it sits inside it
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
a tear in fabric is a rip

explanation.surface: Someone attacks hard fruit that is apparently not yet ready to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words look like an aside, but they hold both the letter source and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is still green has not ripened yet; 'perhaps' flags that green is just one sign of it.

clue.text: Virus strain going round eastern part of tropical country

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus or infection

indicators.note: on a map east is the right-hand side, so the right-hand end of the word is kept

parts.note: its final letter
a strain is a tune, and an aria is a song

explanation.surface: A strain of virus spreading around the eastern region of a hot country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virus strain' reads as one medical phrase but splits into two pieces, with the strain meaning a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a country in south-eastern Europe on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Snack was terrible when cooked, and hard inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so the letter sits among the others
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A snack that tasted awful once cooked, being tough in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese melted on toast, a traditional British snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury light dish of cheese sauce grilled on toast, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: What sailors have on land, or else have at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Sailors get something on land, or else they are stuck on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' sits naturally in a nautical surface, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore leave is time off granted to a ship's crew to go ashore.

clue.text: European talent spotter ignoring United

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a talent scout looks for promising performers
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A continental talent scout passes over Manchester United or some other United side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot comes from Scotland, part of Europe, so the definition is a broad category containing the answer.

clue.text: One patched from time to time

indicators.note: something done from time to time happens at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who gets mended every now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the one in a pack of playing cards, and also a single point in dice.

clue.text: Is Patrick shifting a large amount of cash to fund a start-up?

definitions.text: amount of cash to fund a start-up

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
'a' as written plus L, the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Patrick is moving a big sum of money to back a new company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A large amount of cash' reads as one phrase, but 'a large' joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Risk capital is money invested in a new or speculative business where losses are possible.

clue.text: One taking flight with free ticket east beyond Ireland

parts.note: a pass gives free admission
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
E for east, placed after the previous piece

explanation.surface: A passenger with a free ticket flying east past Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking flight' suggests travel, but the definition is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A passerine is a perching bird such as a sparrow, so it is a creature that flies.

clue.text: Strange old guys held in secure accommodation

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters come out of their usual order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: something held in is enclosed, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to secure something is to get it
guys are men

explanation.surface: Odd elderly men locked up in a secure unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure accommodation' reads as one phrase but 'secure' is a verb in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgement is a place to stay or lodge, an old word for lodging.

clue.text: Everybody repeats what everybody eventually does?

parts.note: all means everybody
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark that everyone keeps repeating what everyone ends up doing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: the two words 'everybody eventually' both start with E, so that phrase itself does what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that alliterate begin with the same sound, which is exactly what this two-word phrase displays.

clue.text: Vessel that is easier to pick up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships

explanation.surface: A query about which boat is easier to lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge for ferrying goods to and from ships, and lighter also means less heavy.

clue.text: Flower finally removed from raised section of garden

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, leaving the rest

parts.note: raised as in raised animals or children, meaning bred

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A bloom taken out of a raised bed in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised section of garden' looks like the definition, a raised bed; but 'raised' is the word that loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower bed is a plot or patch within a garden where plants are grown.

clue.text: Small ship filled with nothing elaborate

indicators.note: something filled with another has it inside

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A little ship stuffed with nothing very fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque describes a highly ornate style, so it means richly decorated or ornate.

clue.text: Mostly wonderful Christmas party?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: magic as an adjective means wonderful

explanation.surface: A cheery comment that a festive party was nearly perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' means a group of people, not a celebration; the question mark signals the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi, the wise men of the Nativity story, are a group of travellers associated with Christmas.

clue.text: Method to get little dog clean

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a method of working
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A technique for getting a puppy clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to clear away spilt liquid or mess, which is to tidy.

clue.text: One greater, flourishing source of fruit

indicators.note: flourishing can mean waving about with a flourish, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something growing bigger and thriving yields produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourishing' suits a growing plant in the surface, which disguises it as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange tree bears citrus, so it is literally a source of that crop.

clue.text: Article in L'Humanité covering northern area of Pas-de-Calais

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: les is a French definite article; L'Humanité is a French newspaper
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A newspaper article reporting on the north of a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a news piece, but it is the grammatical word, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lens is a town in the Pas-de-Calais department of northern France, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Lead scientist primarily taking on variant plants

indicators.note: taking something on means accepting it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a variant is an alternative or other version

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A chief scientist is taking on a different strain of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead scientist' reads as a job title, but 'Lead' is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Potherbs are leafy plants grown for cooking, such as greens added to a pot.

clue.text: Extract provided by author is questionably bordering on unseemly

indicators.note: an extract is a passage taken from a longer text, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: A passage from a writer is dubiously close to indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué describes something slightly indecent or improper, verging on bad taste.

clue.text: Plot to track soldier's drone

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a plot of land is a site; 'to track' means it follows behind

explanation.surface: A scheme to follow a soldier's unmanned aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' suggests an aircraft, but it is the idle male bee, someone who lives off others.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is someone who lives off the work of others without contributing, just like a sponger or freeloader.

clue.text: Show mercy with regard to needing fast time?

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A question about mercy in relation to a time of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and become less harsh, which is showing leniency.
